## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 17, titled *Nikkaḍḍhana* ("Evicting a monk"), establishes that a monk who ejects another monk from a dwelling belonging to the Saṅgha incurs an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*). The text forms part of a pair of rules governing mutual consideration regarding communal lodgings [Hüsken 1997]. Its legal analysis specifies that throwing a monastic or their belongings out of non-communal dwellings, such as an assembly hall or private hut not owned by the Saṅgha, incurs the lesser offense of wrongdoing (*dukkaṭa*) [Hüsken 1997]. The non-offense clauses (*anāpatti*) set out the legal exceptions, defining which disruptive or improper individuals may legitimately be evicted alongside their belongings without fault [Hüsken 1997].
